1.

Through the instant petition, filed by the petitioner seeks anticipatory bail in case FIR No. 0076 dated 17.08.2024 registered under Sections 406, 420 of IPC registered at Police Station Bhargo Camp District Police Commissionerate, Jalandhar.

entities.text: Police Station Bhargo Camp District Police Commissionerate, Jalandhar
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 2. Vide order dated 21.10.2024, passed by this Court, the petitioner was released on interim bail and was directed to join investigation.

Order dated 21.10.2024, passed by this Court, reads as under:
"The instant petition has been filed seeking benefit of pre- arrest bail in case arising out of FIR No.0076 dated 17.08.2024 under Sections 406, 420 of IPC registered at Police Station Bhargo Camp District Police Comissionerate, Jalandhar, Punjab on the basis of a written complaint filed by the complainant-Joginder Singh alleging therein that his daughter Rajwinder Kaur was married with Manpreet Singh who is son of the present petitioner on 05.12.2022.

entities.text: Police Station Bhargo Camp District Police Comissionerate, Jalandhar
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The son of the petitioner was working abroad and 15 days after the wedding, he had gone back.
The daughter of the complainant had to join him.
On 02.02.2023, she suffered a heart attack when she had come to the house of the complainant for the purpose of submission of her visa application and had died.

On request of Manpreet Singh to the effect that he needed money for starting some business upon CRM-M-52052-2024 which the complainant transferred an amount of Rs.15 lakhs in the bank account of his mother-in-law.
The present petitioner Manpreet Singh had assured him to return that amount within a period of three months.

The complainant also alleged that he had spent huge money at the time of marriage of her daughter as istridhan and cash amount of Rs.4,50,000/- had also been given to the petitioner for the purpose of submitting paper of his daughter in the embassy, had also not been returned.

The complainant has prayed for taking Param Pal Singh vs State Of Punjab on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156415478/
1 action against the petitioner and his family members.

entities.text: Param Pal Singh vs State Of Punjab
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Apprehending his arrest, the petitioner moved an application for grant of pre-arrest bail which was dismissed by learned Court of Additional Sessions Judge, Jalandhar vide order dated 10.10.2024.
It is argued by learned counsel for the petitioner that he has been falsely implicated in this case.
There is delay of one year and nine months in registration of FIR from the death of daughter of the complainant.
The amount of Rs.15 lakhs was transferred in the bank account of wife of the petitioner by the complainant as that much amount was due to be payable by him to the son of the petitioner.
The said amount had not been borrowed by the petitioner or his son as alleged and that dispute between the parties is even otherwise a civil nature.
He is ready to join the investigation.
His custodial investigation is not required.
No recovery is to be effected from him.
Therefore, it is urged that he deserves to be extended benefit of bail.
Notice of motion.
At this stage, Power of Attorney has been filed on behalf of the complainant.
Learned State counsel who has advance notice of the petition has submitted that during the course of investigation offence under Section 201 IPC has also been added.
Faced with this situation, learned counsel for the petitioner orally requested that this provision may also be added in the head note as well as prayer clause of the petition.
It is ordered to be so.
Registry is directed to do the needful.

Learned State counsel assisted by learned counsel for the complainant has submitted that there are serious allegations against the petitioner who in connivance with his son had induced the complainant to part with some of Rs.15 lakhs by way of loan and the same would be returned within a period of three months.
It is also CRM-M-52052-2024 2024 BHHG.
MAH t argued that the petitioner has joined investigation but he has not cooperated with the investigation that is why his pre-arrest bail was rejected.
It is therefore, urged that petitioner does not deserve to be extended benefit of pre-arrest bail.
For filing status report, a date is requested.
Adjourned to 05.12.2024.

I n t h e m e a n t i m e , t h e p e t i t i o n e r i s d i r e c t e d t o a p p e a r b e f o r e t h e Investigating/Arresting Officer to join investigation within one week or as and when s u b s e q u e n t l y r e q u i r e d t h e r e a f t e r .
I n t h e e v e n t o f h i s a r r e s t , t h e
Investigating/Arresting Officer shall release the petitioner on interim bail on furnishing personal/surety bonds to his/her satisfaction.

The petitioner shall also abide by the conditions as envisaged under Section 482 (2) of Bharatiya Nagarik Param Pal Singh vs State Of Punjab on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156415478/
2 Suraksha Sanhita (for short BNSS), 2023."
3.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned State counsel, on instructions from the Investigating Officer, has submitted that the petitioner has joined investigation on 09.11.2024 and he is not required for custodial interrogation.

4. Keeping in view the above mentioned facts and circumstances, without commenting on the merits of the case, the present petition is allowed and the order dated 21.10.2024, granting interim bail to the petitioner, is made absolute, subject to the conditions laid down in Section 482(2) of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023.
